c.tagline: Czechia's gritty steel city reborn — blast furnaces turned festival grounds.

taxi.fareNote: Metered — use a ride-hailing app or a phone-booked cab to avoid overpaying.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to all services; 158 reaches the police and 155 the ambulance directly.

avoid.reason: Stodolní Street's bar strip gets rowdy late at night, and the main station and Přívoz area warrant a closer eye on belongings.

hood_desc: The central district and cultural heart around Masaryk Square, with the Ostrava Museum, the New City Hall viewing tower, shops, and restaurants; the most convenient base for visitors.
The legendary bar-and-club street and the blocks around it, packed with pubs, music venues, and late-night crowds; the going-out capital of the city.
Home to Dolní Vítkovice, a colossal former ironworks reborn as a cultural and educational complex with concerts, museums, and the landmark Bolt Tower; industrial heritage at its most dramatic.
A large planned district of Socialist-realist ('Sorela') architecture, leafy parks, and the VŠB technical university; calm, green, and residential.
The Silesian bank across the Ostravice river, home to the Silesian Ostrava Castle and the city zoo; quieter and more suburban in feel.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Czechia.

transit.hours: Trams, trolleybuses, and buses run roughly 4:30am-11pm; a network of night lines runs through the small hours across the city.
transit.note: DPO runs a dense network of trams, trolleybuses, and buses covering the sprawling city and nearby towns; the center is compact but districts like Poruba and Vítkovice are best reached by tram.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless bank card or phone on the reader when boarding, or buy tickets from machines, the MobisTicket/DPO app, or an SMS ticket; validate on boarding. A short ride is about 20 CZK (~$0.90).

transit.m: Train S4 from the airport's own station to Ostrava-Svinov / main station (~30 min)
Airport Express (AE) bus to the central bus station (ÚAN) — free of charge since 2026

tip.r: ~10% for good service in restaurants; round up for taxis and casual spots.

food.name: Smoked Pork with Silesian Dumplings and Cabbage
food.desc: Uzene s knedlikem a zelim: smoked pork with soft potato-bread dumplings and stewed cabbage, the plate that fed generations of miners here.

places.name: Moravska chalupa
places.note: Timber-lined Moravian and Silesian kitchen cooking rustic miners' meals the old way.

places.name: Restaurace Spolek
places.note: Popular Czech restaurant on the bar street doing proper dumplings rather than pub shortcuts.

places.name: Scansen restaurant
places.note: Folk-style dining room built around regional recipes and big traditional portions.

food.name: Silesian Gulas
food.desc: Dark beef goulash cooked with beer, caraway and onion, served with bread dumplings or in a hollowed loaf. Heavier and darker than the Prague version.

places.name: Restaurace Spolek
places.note: Reliable, well-reviewed goulash with a good beer list at the centre of the nightlife strip.

places.name: Moravska chalupa
places.note: Traditional recipes and slow cooking; goulash is the house benchmark dish.

places.name: Design restaurace Jan Maria
places.note: Smarter kitchen that keeps a refined take on Czech classics alongside modern plates.

food.name: Ostravska Klobasa
food.desc: Coarse smoked sausage grilled over charcoal and served with rye bread, mustard and horseradish. Ostrava's default street food.

places.name: Stodolni Street stalls
places.note: Grill vendors work the bar street all evening; the classic late-night stop.

places.name: Masarykovo namesti markets
places.note: Main-square market stalls sell grilled sausage and smoked meats, best at seasonal markets.

places.name: Moravska chalupa
places.note: Sit-down version with cabbage and dumplings if you want it as a full meal.

food.name: Slezska Kyselica
food.desc: Silesian sour soup of sauerkraut juice, potatoes, mushrooms and sausage, thickened with cream. A true regional dish you rarely see elsewhere in Czechia.

places.name: Moravska chalupa
places.note: One of the few places keeping the older Silesian soups on the menu year-round.

places.name: Scansen restaurant
places.note: Regional cooking with country soups served in bread bowls.

places.name: Restaurace Spolek
places.note: Rotating daily soups that usually include a Silesian sour or cabbage soup.

food.name: Miners' Plate and Smoked Meats
food.desc: Hornicky talir: a heavy platter of smoked meat, sausage, crackling, pickles and bread, the coal-town meal Ostrava built its identity on.

places.name: Moravska chalupa
places.note: Explicitly serves mine-worker style meals cooked by traditional methods.

places.name: Scansen restaurant
places.note: Big shared boards of smoked meat and pickles suited to a group and a few beers.

places.name: Restaurace Spolek
places.note: Good for beer snacks: utopenci, nakladany hermelin and smoked pork knuckle.

food.name: Smazeny Syr and Pub Classics
food.desc: Breaded fried Edam with tartare sauce and fries, plus svickova and roast duck. The comfort food every Ostrava pub is measured against.

places.name: Moravska chalupa
places.note: Singled out in guides for its fried cheese and traditional Czech mains.

places.name: Restaurace Spolek
places.note: Late kitchen hours make it the go-to for pub classics after a night out.

places.name: HogoFogo Bistro
places.note: Modern bistro that reworks Czech staples with better ingredients.

food.name: Ostravar Beer
food.desc: The city's own brewery, making a firm, slightly bitter Czech lager plus dark and unfiltered versions poured across Moravian-Silesian pubs.

places.name: Ostravar Brewery
places.note: The working city brewery, with tours and tastings of the hometown lager.

places.name: Restaurace Spolek
places.note: Well-kept taps and Czech food to go with them, in the middle of the bar district.

places.name: Stodolni Street pubs
places.note: Dozens of bars on one street, most pouring Ostravar and other Czech lagers cheaply.

food.name: Slivovice and Moravian Wine
food.desc: Plum brandy drunk as a shot before or after dinner, plus crisp whites from the Moravian vineyards a couple of hours south.

places.name: HogoFogo Bistro
places.note: Bar-led bistro with a serious drinks list including Czech spirits and Moravian wine.

places.name: Moravska chalupa
places.note: Traditional house slivovice served the way locals take it, ice-cold and neat.

places.name: Stodolni Street bars
places.note: Wine bars and cellars among the pubs, good for a Moravian tasting flight.

landmarks: Dolní Vítkovice (Lower Vítkovice)
A colossal former ironworks transformed into Europe's most striking industrial playground, where blast furnaces, gasometers and pipes now host concerts, museums and festivals.
Bolt Tower
The futuristic glass extension crowning Blast Furnace No. 1, named for sprinter Usain Bolt, with a skywalk café gazing over Ostrava's rusted industrial cathedral.
New City Hall Viewing Tower
The tallest city-hall tower in Czechia lifts visitors 73 meters above Ostrava for panoramas stretching from the Beskydy Mountains to Poland.
Landek Park Mining Museum
The country's largest mining museum, where retired miners guide you down the Anselm pit and vintage machinery recalls three centuries of Silesian coal.
Silesian Ostrava Castle
A 13th-century castle rebuilt after mining subsidence sank it several meters, now hosting exhibitions, an aquarium of local fish and lively summer festivals.
Masaryk Square (Masarykovo náměstí)
Ostrava's historic marketplace since the 13th century, ringed by pastel burgher houses, the old town hall museum and a baroque Marian plague column.
Cathedral of the Divine Saviour
The second-largest church in Moravia and Silesia, a neo-Renaissance basilica of 1889 whose twin towers preside over the city's café-lined boulevards.
Stodolní Street
The legendary 'street that never sleeps,' packing dozens of bars, clubs and music venues into a few blocks of Ostrava's gritty-turned-hip nightlife district.
Ostrava Zoo
One of Czechia's largest zoos, a hillside botanical park sheltering elephants, lemurs and rare Amur leopards amid extensive woodland walking trails.
Ema Slag Heap (Halda Ema)
A smoldering man-made hill of mine tailings whose warm, faintly sulfurous summit offers Ostrava's quirkiest viewpoint over chimneys, spires and distant mountains.

train.note: Ostrava sits close to both the Polish and Slovak borders and is a genuine international junction - trains run north to Kraków and Warsaw and south to Vienna and Budapest. Prague is about 3 hours away with three competing operators, so fares are unusually cheap. Ostrava hlavní nádraží and Ostrava-Svinov both take long-distance services; check which one your ticket names.

bus.note: Coaches use the ÚAN Ostrava terminal. RegioJet and FlixBus run to Kraków in about 3 hours and to Prague, Brno and Vienna. Carry your passport or EU ID card, though all these are internal Schengen crossings.

ferry.note: Czechia is landlocked and Ostrava's rivers carry no passenger service, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Štramberk
half.blurb: A medieval watchtower and gingerbread-scented wooden folk houses sit in the Beskydy foothills about thirty minutes away.

half.name: Hukvaldy
half.blurb: A ruined hilltop castle and the birthplace of composer Leoš Janáček lie roughly thirty minutes southeast of Ostrava.

half.name: Pustevny
half.blurb: Mountain-ridge hiking trails and Art Nouveau timber chalets in the Beskydy Mountains are about an hour away.

half.name: Český Těšín
half.blurb: A border town split from Poland's Cieszyn by the Olza River sits roughly forty minutes east of Ostrava.
